items.title: 52060_Eddie Barefield oral history interview
items.q: we had Hilton Jefferson on first ... had Ike Quebec on one tenor and Sam Taylor on the other tenor.

ctx.x: This was the late '50s, wasn't it?

Something like that. And we played -- he had a band, a nice, a marvelous band with Pearl Bailey and Louie Belson on drums, and he had Sam Taylor and me and Sammy Most and George Dorsey, and we played around. But Don was a very unsung hero of music. I think he was one of the greatest, you know, all around musicians because he could play any instrument in the orchestra, you know. He played -- and when he was with the Cottonpickers, whoever was missing, he would just sit down and play the book, trumpet, trombone,…
Well, he has been given credit for being, you know, really shaping the whole idea of the big band arrangement.
